# 02.2 Headings and Paragraphs: Writing Text Content

Now that you know how to add settings to your elements with attributes, it's time to fill the page with actual content. The two most common text elements are **headings** and **paragraphs** — they follow the exact same open—content—close pattern you already know.

## Headings: Six Levels of Importance

HTML gives you six heading tags, from `<h1>` (most important) down to `<h6>` (least important). Think of them as labels for sections: `<h1>` is the page title, `<h2>` is a major section, `<h3>` a subsection, and so on. Every heading is a **block-level** element — it takes up its own line and pushes the next element down.

```html
<h1>Welcome to My Website</h1>
<h2>About Me</h2>
<h3>My Hobbies</h3>
```

All headings use the same open—content—close pattern: `<h1>` opens, the heading text goes in the middle, `</h1>` closes. Never skip the closing tag — otherwise, the browser treats everything after as part of the heading, and your page layout breaks.

## Paragraphs: The Default Text Container

A paragraph is written with the `<p>` tag and is also block-level. It automatically adds a bit of space before and after, so your text reads naturally, like paragraphs in a book.

```html
<p>This is a paragraph. It can contain several sentences, and the browser will wrap them appropriately. Without the closing tag, the next element would be swallowed up.</p>
```

Same rule applies: opening tag, content, closing tag. If you forget `</p>`, the text that follows becomes part of the same paragraph — your structure collapses.

## Putting It All Together

Here's a complete minimal HTML page that uses both headings and paragraphs:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <title>My Page</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <h1>My First Web Page</h1>
    <p>This is my very first paragraph. I am learning HTML step by step.</p>
    <p>This is another paragraph. Each one needs its own opening and closing tag.</p>
  </body>
</html>
```

Now it's your turn. Open `index.html` and build your own page from scratch.

```code_challenge_proposal
In this exercise, the student needs to write a complete HTML document in index.html. The page must start with <!DOCTYPE html> and include the full skeleton: <html>, <head> with a <title>, and <body>. Inside the <body>, the student must add exactly one <h1> heading with the text 'My First Web Page', one <h2> heading with the text 'About Me', and two <p> paragraphs with any text of their choice. All tags must be properly opened and closed, and all visible content must be inside the <body> element. The file index.html will be the place where the student writes the code.
```
